examples.en: That greeting is an expression people use out of custom.
Try to break away from conventional ways of thinking.
These days most holiday greetings are just customary.
If you only use stock expressions, your writing gets boring.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 줄거리가 너무 관습적이라서 새롭지 않아요.
examples.en: This movie's plot is so conventional that it doesn't feel fresh.
Try finding an unconventional method.

explain: 오랜 습관이나 관례에 따라 하는 것을 말해요. '전통적'은 중립적이거나 좋게 들리지만, '관습적'은 생각 없이 틀에 박힌 대로 한다는 느낌이 담길 때가 많아요. 반대 느낌은 '독창적', '파격적'이에요.
explain_en: It describes doing something according to long-standing habit or convention. '전통적' sounds neutral or positive, while '관습적' often carries a feel of doing things by rote without thinking. The opposite feel is '독창적' or '파격적'.

examples.ko: 두 나라 군대가 국경에서 교전을 벌였어요.
examples.en: The armies of the two countries fought at the border.

examples.ko: 교전 때문에 많은 사람이 집을 떠났어요.
examples.en: Many people left their homes because of the fighting.
The news keeps reporting on the fighting.

examples.ko: 교전이 멈추고 나서야 마을에 평화가 왔어요.
examples.en: Peace only came to the village after the fighting stopped.

examples.ko: 어젯밤 교전으로 군인 몇 명이 다쳤어요.
examples.en: Several soldiers were hurt in last night's clash.
You cannot enter the combat zone.

explain: '전쟁'은 나라 사이의 크고 긴 싸움이고, '교전'은 무기를 들고 실제로 맞붙어 싸우는 순간에 초점이 있어요. 뉴스에서 '교전이 벌어지다', '교전이 멈추다'처럼 자주 들려요.
explain_en: 전쟁 is a big, long war between nations, while 교전 focuses on the moment armed forces actually clash. You often hear it in the news as 교전이 벌어지다 or 교전이 멈추다.

examples.en: That is far too outdated an idea.
That advertisement is a bit outdated.

examples.ko: 아버지의 구시대적 생각이 답답할 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes my father's old-fashioned thinking is frustrating.
It's an outdated rule, so everyone says we should change it.

examples.ko: 이런 구시대적 제도가 아직도 있다니 놀라워요.
examples.en: I'm surprised that an outdated system like this still exists.

examples.ko: 구시대적 방법으로는 요즘 손님을 잡기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to attract today's customers with outdated methods.

explain: 생각, 제도, 관행, 방식이 시대에 뒤떨어졌다고 비판할 때 써요. 물건이나 스타일이 예스러울 때 쓰는 '구식'보다 평가가 더 강해요. 보통 '구시대적 발상', '구시대적 관행'처럼 명사 앞에 붙여요.
explain_en: Use it to criticize ideas, systems, practices, or methods as behind the times. It is a stronger judgment than '구식', which is used for old-fashioned things or styles. It is usually placed before a noun, as in '구시대적 발상' or '구시대적 관행'.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 근대적인 계획에 따라 만들어졌어요.
examples.en: This city was built following a modern plan.
The modern education system began at that time.

examples.ko: 그 공장은 근대적 설비를 갖추고 있어요.
examples.en: That factory is equipped with modern facilities.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 근대적 가치관을 잘 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This novel shows modern values well.
The design of this building is very modern in style.
I was surprised that my grandmother's thinking was so modern.

explain: '근대적 + 명사'로 쓰고, '근대적이다'처럼 서술어로도 써요. '근대'는 옛날과 오늘날 사이의 시기라서, '근대적'은 '현대적'(지금 느낌)과 다르게 그 시기의 제도나 생각을 가리킬 때 써요.
explain_en: It is used before a noun as '근대적 + noun' and also as a predicate like '근대적이다'. '근대' is the period between old times and today, so '근대적' points to systems or ideas of that period, unlike '현대적', which means modern in today's sense.

examples.en: A civilized country must protect people's rights.
He introduced Korea as a civilized country.
Even in civilized countries, environmental problems are a big task.
Obeying the law is the basis of a civilized country.

examples.ko: 어떤 나라를 문명국가라고 부를 수 있을까요?
examples.en: What kind of country can we call a civilized country?

examples.ko: 문명국가는 교육과 법이 잘 갖춰져 있어요.
examples.en: Civilized countries have well-established education and laws.

explain: 경제력보다 법, 교육, 인권 같은 사회 수준을 강조하는 말이에요. 경제 수준을 말할 때는 보통 '선진국'을 써요.
explain_en: This word stresses a society's level in law, education and human rights rather than its economic power. When talking about economic level, people usually use '선진국'.

examples.ko: 그 의원은 잘못을 인정하고 백의종군하겠다고 밝혔어요.
examples.en: The lawmaker admitted his mistake and said he would serve without any post.

examples.ko: 그는 선거에서 지고도 백의종군해서 후배를 도왔어요.
examples.en: Even after losing the election, he stayed on without a title and helped his juniors.
General Yi Sun-sin once served without rank.
There were calls for him to take responsibility and serve without a post.

examples.ko: 당 대표는 백의종군하며 선거를 돕기로 했어요.
examples.en: The party leader decided to help with the election without any official post.

examples.ko: 높은 자리에서 내려와 백의종군하기는 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It is not easy to step down from a high post and serve without a title.

explain: 원래는 벼슬 없이 군대를 따라가 싸운다는 역사 이야기에서 나온 말이에요. 요즘은 정치나 스포츠 뉴스에서 직책을 내려놓고 일반 구성원으로 돕겠다고 할 때 써요.
explain_en: It comes from the historical idea of following the army and fighting without any official rank. Today it appears in politics and sports news when someone gives up their post and says they will help as an ordinary member.

examples.ko: 한복의 모양은 시대에 따라 조금씩 변천해 왔어요.
examples.en: The shape of hanbok has gradually changed over the eras.
I studied how Hangul spelling rules have changed over time.

examples.ko: 도시의 모습이 변천하는 과정을 사진으로 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see the city's changing appearance over time in photos.
Food culture changes along with society.

examples.ko: 오랜 세월 변천한 이 마을의 모습이 신기해요.
examples.en: It's fascinating how this village has changed over the long years.

examples.ko: 유행은 계속 변천하기 때문에 따라가기 힘들어요.
examples.en: Trends keep shifting, so it's hard to keep up.

explain: '변하다'보다 역사, 문화, 제도처럼 오랜 시간 단계적으로 달라지는 흐름에 써요. 일상에서 기분이나 날씨가 바뀔 때는 '변하다'를 써요. '변천사'라는 말도 많이 써요.
explain_en: Compared with '변하다', it fits long, step-by-step changes in history, culture or systems. For mood or weather changes in daily life, use '변하다'. The word '변천사' (history of changes) is also common.

examples.ko: 할아버지의 봉건적 생각을 바꾸기는 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It's not easy to change Grandfather's feudal way of thinking.

examples.ko: 봉건적 신분 제도에서는 태어난 집안이 중요했어요.
examples.en: Under a feudal class system, the family you were born into mattered.
The atmosphere at that company is far too feudal.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 봉건적 질서에 맞서는 여자가 주인공이에요.
examples.en: The heroine of this novel is a woman who stands against the feudal order.
Feudal customs are gradually disappearing.
I was told my way of speaking is too old-fashioned and authoritarian.

explain: 역사 수업에서는 봉건 사회를 가리키고, 일상에서는 윗사람 말만 따르는 낡고 권위적인 분위기를 비판할 때 써요. '봉건적인', '봉건적이다'처럼 쓰기도 해요. '권위적'과 비슷하지만 더 낡았다는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: In history class it refers to feudal society, and in daily life it criticizes an outdated, authoritarian atmosphere where people just obey superiors. It can also appear as '봉건적인' or '봉건적이다'. It is similar to '권위적' but carries a stronger sense of being outdated.

examples.en: He passed away last month.
News was reported that the president had passed away.

examples.ko: 원로 화가가 서거하신 날에 많은 제자가 모였어요.
examples.en: Many students gathered on the day the senior painter passed away.

examples.ko: 그가 서거하기 전까지 책을 계속 썼어요.
examples.en: He kept writing books until he passed away.

examples.ko: 왕이 서거하자 온 나라가 슬픔에 잠겼어요.
examples.en: When the king died, the whole country sank into grief.
A great writer has passed away, and everyone feels the loss.

explain: '죽다'의 높임 중에서도 아주 격식 있는 말로, 뉴스에서 대통령이나 원로처럼 존경받는 인물에게 써요. 가족이나 가까운 어른에게는 '돌아가셨어요'가 자연스러워요. '서거하셨다'처럼 '-시-'를 붙여 쓸 때가 많아요.
explain_en: This is a very formal honorific for dying, used in the news for respected figures such as presidents and senior figures. For family or close elders '돌아가셨어요' sounds natural. It is often used with '-시-', as in '서거하셨다'.

examples.en: A student representative read the declaration.
We learn about the declaration of independence in history class.

examples.ko: 환경 단체가 지구를 지키자는 선언문을 발표했어요.
examples.en: An environmental group released a declaration urging people to protect the Earth.
Those who agree with the declaration, please write your name.

examples.ko: 동아리 선언문을 모두 함께 소리 내어 읽었어요.
examples.en: We all read the club's declaration aloud together.
The declaration is short but powerful.

explain: '독립 선언문', '인권 선언문'처럼 중요한 약속이나 주장을 공식적으로 밝힐 때 써요. 개인의 다짐은 '다짐'이나 '각오'를 더 자주 써요. '성명서'는 입장을 알리는 글이라서 조금 달라요.
explain_en: It is used for formally stating an important promise or claim, as in '독립 선언문' and '인권 선언문'. For personal resolutions people say '다짐' or '각오'. '성명서' is a statement of a position, so it differs slightly.

examples.en: The army recaptured the city it had lost.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 빼앗겼던 섬을 수복하려고 애썼어요.
examples.en: That country tried hard to reclaim the island it had lost.

examples.ko: 사라진 영토를 수복하는 데 십 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took ten years to reclaim the lost territory.
When the lost land was reclaimed, people cheered.
The government announced that it had retaken the occupied area.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 작년에 수복해서 아직 복구 중이에요.
examples.en: This area was retaken last year, so it is still being rebuilt.

explain: '되찾다'와 비슷하지만 '수복하다'는 점령당했거나 잃은 땅, 지역에 주로 써서 글이나 뉴스 느낌이 나요. 일상에서는 '되찾다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '땅/도시/지역을 수복하다'처럼 목적어는 장소가 와요.
explain_en: It is close to '되찾다' (to get back), but '수복하다' is mainly used for occupied or lost land and regions, and has a news or written feel. In everyday speech '되찾다' sounds much more natural. The object is usually a place, as in '땅/도시/지역을 수복하다'.

examples.en: The investigation team arrived at the scene and started looking into it.

examples.ko: 경찰은 수사진을 두 배로 늘리기로 했어요.
examples.en: The police decided to double the size of the investigation team.

examples.ko: 새로 꾸린 수사진에 전문가가 여러 명 있어요.
examples.en: There are several experts on the newly formed investigation team.
According to the investigators, the results will come out soon.

examples.ko: 이 사건은 수사진도 처음 보는 경우라고 해요.
examples.en: They say even the investigators have never seen a case like this.
The whole investigation team checked the materials all night.

explain: '의료진', '취재진', '경영진'처럼 '-진'이 붙어서 사람들의 팀 전체를 가리켜요. 한 사람은 '수사관'이라고 하고, 뉴스에서는 '수사진이 꾸려지다', '수사진을 보강하다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: Like '의료진' (medical staff), '취재진' (press corps) and '경영진' (management), the '-진' ending refers to a whole team of people. One person is called '수사관' (investigator). In the news you often see '수사진이 꾸려지다' (a team is formed) and '수사진을 보강하다' (reinforce the team).

examples.ko: 이 성당은 순교한 신자들을 기리려고 지었어요.
examples.en: This cathedral was built to honor the believers who died for their faith.
I visited a museum that introduces the history of martyrdom.

examples.ko: 그는 끝까지 믿음을 버리지 않고 순교에 이르렀어요.
examples.en: He never gave up his faith and ended up a martyr.

examples.ko: 순교 현장에는 매년 많은 순례자가 찾아와요.
examples.en: Many pilgrims visit the site of martyrdom every year.
Reading the story of martyrdom made me solemn.

examples.ko: 순교를 기념하는 미사가 오늘 저녁에 있어요.
examples.en: There is a Mass commemorating the martyrdom this evening.

explain: 종교, 특히 기독교 역사 이야기에서 쓰는 말이라 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 나와요. 믿음을 지키다 죽은 사람은 '순교자'라고 해요. 나라를 위해 목숨을 바친 경우에는 '순국'을 써서 서로 달라요.
explain_en: It belongs to religious talk, especially Christian history, and rarely comes up in daily conversation. A person who died for their faith is a '순교자'. Dying for one's country uses '순국' instead, so the two are different.

examples.en: At church, they teach the Ten Commandments to children.
The Ten Commandments are a famous teaching from the Bible.
Among the Ten Commandments, there is the saying 'Do not steal.'

examples.ko: 우리 가족은 건강 십계명을 만들어 냉장고에 붙였어요.
examples.en: Our family made ten health rules and stuck them on the fridge.

examples.ko: 운전자 십계명을 읽고 안전하게 운전하기로 했어요.
examples.en: I read the ten rules for drivers and decided to drive safely.

examples.ko: 이 책에는 공부 잘하는 십계명이 실려 있어요.
examples.en: This book contains ten rules for studying well.

explain: 원래는 종교 이야기에 나오는 말이지만 '건강 십계명', '운전 십계명'처럼 꼭 지켜야 할 규칙 모음에도 써요. 이런 쓰임은 광고나 안내문에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It originally belongs to religious talk, but it is also used for a set of rules to follow, as in '건강 십계명' (ten health rules) or '운전 십계명' (ten driving rules). You often see this use in ads and notices.

examples.en: The residents joined forces and solved the problem.
The harder the times, the more we need to stand together.
It's a group that works in solidarity with students from other countries.
The small shops banded together and held an event.
We want to stand with the victims.
Thanks to joining together, our strength grew.

explain: 사람들이 같은 목표나 처지 때문에 서로 힘을 모아 함께할 때 써요. 단순히 '같이하다'보다 서로 책임을 나누는 무게가 있어요. 명사 '연대'는 '연대 의식', '연대 책임'처럼 써요.
explain_en: For people pooling strength because of a shared goal or situation. It carries more weight than plain '같이하다', since it implies shared responsibility. The noun '연대' appears in '연대 의식' (sense of solidarity) and '연대 책임' (joint responsibility).

examples.ko: 그 학자는 정치 싸움에 져서 먼 섬으로 유배됐어요.
examples.en: The scholar lost a political fight and was exiled to a distant island.

examples.ko: 유배된 선비는 매일 편지를 써서 가족에게 보냈어요.
examples.en: The exiled scholar wrote letters every day and sent them to his family.
He was unjustly exiled and spent ten years there.

examples.ko: 왕의 미움을 받은 신하가 유배되는 이야기예요.
examples.en: It's a story about a subject who incurs the king's hatred and is exiled.

examples.ko: 유배돼 있는 동안에도 그는 책 읽기를 멈추지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even while in exile, he never stopped reading.
If his wrongdoing came to light, he could have been exiled.

explain: '유배를 가다'가 가는 사람에게 초점을 두는 데 비해, '유배되다'는 처벌로 보내진다는 느낌이 더 커요. 보내는 쪽을 주어로 하면 '유배를 보내다'라고 해요. 역사 이야기에서만 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: '유배를 가다' focuses on the person going, whereas '유배되다' has a stronger sense of being sent away as punishment. With the sender as the subject, you say '유배를 보내다'. It is used only in historical contexts.

examples.ko: 임진왜란 때 백성들이 스스로 의병으로 나서서 싸웠어요.
examples.en: During the Imjin War, ordinary people stepped forward on their own as volunteer soldiers.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 의병이 활동한 지역을 지도에서 찾았어요.
examples.en: In history class, we found on the map the areas where the volunteer armies were active.

examples.ko: 의병들은 정식 군인이 아니었지만 나라를 위해 나섰어요.
examples.en: The volunteer soldiers weren't regular soldiers, but they stepped up for the country.

examples.ko: 마을 사람들이 의병을 모집한다는 소식이 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: News spread that the villagers were recruiting a volunteer army.

examples.ko: 의병 활동을 기념하는 박물관이 우리 동네에 있어요.
examples.en: There is a museum in my town commemorating the volunteer army's activities.
I heard my grandfather's grandfather took part in the volunteer army.

explain: 나라가 위기일 때 백성이 스스로 모여 만든 군대나 그 군인을 말하고, '정규군'과 대비해서 써요. 주로 역사 수업이나 역사 이야기에서 만나는 말이에요.
explain_en: It refers to a volunteer army that ordinary people formed on their own when the country was in danger, or to a soldier in it, and it is contrasted with the '정규군' (regular army). You mostly meet it in history classes and historical stories.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 갈등이 결국 전면전으로 번졌어요.
examples.en: The conflict between the two countries finally spread into all-out war.

examples.ko: 두 회사가 가격 인하 전면전에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: The two companies have entered an all-out price-cutting war.

examples.ko: 선거를 앞두고 두 정당이 전면전을 벌이고 있어요.
examples.en: Ahead of the election, the two parties are going head to head.

examples.ko: 이번 경기는 양 팀의 전면전이 될 것 같아요.
examples.en: This match looks like it will be an all-out clash between the two teams.

examples.ko: 이 문제로 전면전까지 갈 필요는 없어요.
examples.en: There's no need to go to all-out war over this issue.
An all-out fight would hurt both sides, so they started negotiating.

explain: 원래는 모든 힘을 쏟아 싸우는 전쟁을 말하지만, 회사 경쟁이나 정치 싸움처럼 정면으로 크게 맞붙는 상황에도 비유로 써요. 일부 지역에서만 벌이는 싸움은 '국지전'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Originally it means a war in which everything is thrown into the fight, but it is also used figuratively for any situation where two sides clash head-on, like business competition or political fights. A fight limited to one area is called '국지전' (a local war).

examples.en: The army is stationed near the border.

examples.ko: 그 부대는 작년부터 이 도시에 주둔했어요.
examples.en: That unit has been stationed in this city since last year.
The soldiers will be stationed in the mountains.

examples.ko: 마을에 주둔하는 군인들이 시장에서 장을 봐요.
examples.en: The soldiers stationed in the village shop at the market.

examples.ko: 부대는 겨울 동안 여기에 주둔하고 있어요.
examples.en: The unit is stationed here for the winter.
People were worried because foreign troops were stationed there.

explain: 주어는 거의 군대나 부대예요. 장소 뒤에는 '에'를 붙여서 '국경에 주둔하다'라고 해요. 사람이 잠시 머무는 일에는 '머무르다'를 써요.
explain_en: The subject is almost always an army or a unit. Put 에 after the place, as in '국경에 주둔하다'. For a person staying somewhere briefly, use 머무르다.

examples.en: The soldiers advanced toward the enemy camp.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 결승전을 향해 진격하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our team is charging toward the final.
The army kept advancing even in the fog.
The general ordered them to advance at dawn.
The unit that was advancing west stopped.
The commander said he would advance at daybreak.

explain: 진격하다는 군대가 적을 향해 용감하게 앞으로 나아갈 때 써요. 스포츠나 게임 이야기에서 기세 좋게 이기며 올라가는 것을 말할 때도 비유로 써요. 일상에서 그냥 앞으로 가는 것은 '나아가다', '가다'를 써요.
explain_en: It describes an army moving boldly toward the enemy. In sports or game talk, it can be used figuratively for winning and moving up with momentum. For ordinary moving forward in daily life, use 나아가다 or 가다.

examples.ko: 전쟁이 길어지자 징집 대상 나이가 낮아졌어요.
examples.en: As the war dragged on, the age of those subject to conscription was lowered.

examples.ko: 그는 갑작스러운 징집 통보를 받고 학교를 떠났어요.
examples.en: He received a sudden conscription notice and left school.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 일제강점기의 강제 징집에 대해 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class, we learned about forced conscription during the Japanese colonial period.

examples.ko: 징집을 피하려고 외국으로 떠난 사람들이 있었어요.
examples.en: There were people who left for other countries to avoid being drafted.

examples.ko: 징집 통지서가 나오기 전까지 가족은 아무것도 몰랐어요.
examples.en: The family knew nothing until the draft notice arrived.
A debate broke out over the draft age.

explain: 나라나 군대가 사람들을 군인으로 불러 모으는 일이에요. 비슷한 '징병'과 함께 나오는 일이 많고, 개인이 군대에 들어가는 일은 '입대'라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a state or army calling people up to serve as soldiers. It often appears together with the similar word '징병', and an individual joining the military is called '입대'.

examples.en: Our school marks its 100th anniversary this year.
We get a day off on the company's founding anniversary.

examples.ko: 창립 멤버는 지금도 같이 일하고 있어요.
examples.en: The founding members still work together.

examples.ko: 동아리 창립 모임이 내일 저녁에 있어요.
examples.en: The club's founding meeting is tomorrow evening.
They held a big party to celebrate the founding.
The founding spirit of this shop is honesty.

explain: '설립'은 법적으로 기관을 세우는 절차에 가깝고, '창립'은 단체나 회사가 처음 시작된 순간과 그 뜻을 기념할 때 많이 써요. 혼자 사업을 시작하면 '창업'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 설립 leans toward the legal act of setting up an institution, while 창립 is often used for the moment a group or company began and its meaning, as in anniversaries. Starting a business on your own is 창업.

examples.en: The new CEO promised change in the inaugural speech.
I listened to the president's inaugural address on the radio.
The principal's inaugural speech was short but moving.

examples.ko: 취임사에 쓸 내용을 며칠째 고민하고 있어요.
examples.en: I've been thinking for days about what to put in my inaugural speech.

examples.ko: 신임 선생님이 첫날 간단한 취임사를 하셨어요.
examples.en: The new teacher gave a brief inaugural speech on the first day.
The inaugural speech was long, so people got bored.

explain: 새로 일을 맡은 사람이 하는 인사 연설이에요. '취임사를 하다/발표하다'로 쓰고, 떠나는 사람이 하는 말은 '이임사', 물러나는 사람이 하는 말은 '퇴임사'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the greeting speech given by someone taking on a new post. It is used as '취임사를 하다/발표하다', while the speech of a person leaving a post is '이임사' and that of one retiring is '퇴임사'.

examples.ko: 판결문에는 재판부가 그렇게 판단한 이유가 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The written judgment explains why the court decided that way.

examples.ko: 판결문을 읽어 보니 내용이 생각보다 복잡했어요.
examples.en: When I read the written judgment, it was more complicated than I expected.
When the written judgment comes out, the news reports it right away.

examples.ko: 이 판결문은 인터넷에서 누구나 찾아볼 수 있어요?
examples.en: Can anyone look up this written judgment online?
The lawyer checked part of the written judgment again.
It's fine to read only the summary of the judgment first.

explain: '판결'은 재판의 결론이고, '판결문'은 그 결론과 이유를 적은 문서예요. '판결이 나다, 판결을 내리다'처럼 말하고, 문서는 '판결문을 읽다, 쓰다'처럼 말해요. 뉴스에서 '판결문에 따르면'이라는 표현이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '판결' is the court's conclusion, while '판결문' is the document that records the conclusion and the reasons. You say '판결이 나다' or '판결을 내리다' for the decision, and '판결문을 읽다' or '쓰다' for the document. The phrase '판결문에 따르면' (according to the judgment) is common in the news.

en: judge; rule on a case; give a verdict

examples.en: The court ruled on the case today.
The judge rules based on the evidence.

examples.ko: 판결할 때는 모든 사실을 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to check all the facts when you pass judgment.

examples.ko: 재판부가 무죄로 판결하면 피고는 바로 풀려나요.
examples.en: If the court rules not guilty, the defendant is released right away.
This issue is hard to settle in court.

examples.ko: 법원이 어떻게 판결할지 모두 기다리고 있어요.
examples.en: Everyone is waiting to see how the court will rule.

explain: 판결하다는 재판에서 쓰는 말이라 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 써요. 일상에서 무언가를 정할 때는 '결정하다'나 '정하다'를 써요. 보통 '판결을 내리다'처럼 명사와 같이 말해요.
explain_en: This is a courtroom word and rarely appears in everyday talk. For ordinary decisions Koreans say '결정하다' or '정하다'. It is usually paired with the noun, as in '판결을 내리다'.

examples.en: The lawmakers vote on the bill this afternoon.
Opinions were divided, so we decided to put it to a vote.

examples.ko: 반장을 뽑을 때 손을 들어 표결했어요.
examples.en: When choosing the class president, we voted by raising hands.
To hold a vote, you first have to decide the agenda item.

examples.ko: 이 안건은 다음 주에 표결할 예정이에요.
examples.en: This item is scheduled to be voted on next week.
Sometimes they decide by applause without voting.

explain: '투표하다'는 선거나 여럿이 고를 때 널리 쓰고, '표결하다'는 회의나 국회에서 안건을 찬성과 반대로 결정할 때 써요. 뉴스에서는 '표결에 부치다', '표결 처리'처럼 명사 '표결'로도 많이 나와요.
explain_en: '투표하다' is used widely for elections or any group choice, while '표결하다' is for deciding an agenda item by yes or no votes in a meeting or the National Assembly. In the news the noun '표결' is also common, as in '표결에 부치다' and '표결 처리'.

examples.en: The navy fleet entered the port.
In the movie, the space fleet protected the Earth.

examples.ko: 이순신 장군의 함대는 바다에서 크게 이겼어요.
examples.en: General Yi Sun-sin's fleet won a great victory at sea.

examples.ko: 배 열 척으로 이루어진 함대를 만들었어요.
examples.en: They built a fleet made up of ten ships.
I saw a model of an old fleet at the museum.
The fleet commander gave the order to set sail.

explain: 역사 이야기나 전쟁·우주 영화에서 자주 나와요. 배가 많이 모여 있어도 군함이 아니면 보통 '선단'이라고 해요. '우주 함대'처럼 상상 속 이야기에도 써요.
explain_en: It comes up often in history and in war or space movies. A group of many ships that are not warships is usually called '선단'. It is also used in imagined stories, as in '우주 함대'.
